organizations.name: National Resistance Front
organizations.notes: Founded Aug 2021 by Ahmad Massoud after Kabul fell; largest/most active anti-Taliban group; fought <1,000 men vs ~35,000 Taliban/TTP/AQ/foreign fighters in Panjshir 15 Aug–6 Sept 2021; now guerrilla phase in mountains; seeks recognition of Taliban as terror group, recognition of democratic forces, and material support (no foreign boots).

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Massoud: more extreme than the 1990s because integrated with AQ and trained by regional agencies; intermarried with AQ; building ~5 jihadi madrasas per district (~2,000); offered Massoud foreign ministry; refused last call for peace in Panjshir.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda
organizations.notes: Killed Ahmad Shah Massoud 9 Sept 2001; Arab AQ fighters filmed joining Panjshir assault 2021; 'localized' jihad via Taliban/TTP/Ansarullah/IMU franchises; many Taliban members are AQ; UN: camps, safe houses, madrasas, media centre, weapons depot in Panjshir.

events.description: Al-Qaeda assassinates Ahmad Shah Massoud two days before 9/11
Kabul falls; Massoud refuses evacuation offers (Macron, Pakistan, Tajikistan) and moves to Panjshir; makes last call for peace, refused by Taliban; founds NRF and calls uprising

Panjshir falls after ~3 weeks: <1,000 NRF fighters vs ~35,000 Taliban with TTP, al-Qaeda Arab fighters, Tajik/Uzbek/Pakistani fighters; NRF ran out of RPG, rifle and PK ammunition; no mines due to treaty
Massoud leaves Panjshir at commanders' request to seek ammunition from Tajikistan; valley falls in his absence
Taliban leader decrees women may no longer study medicine
US small teams via Tajikistan join Northern Alliance; most of Afghanistan liberated in ~3 weeks
DDR (disarmament, demobilization, reintegration) programme disarms Panjshir/Northern Alliance fighters; later APRP
Massoud warns US embassy and Afghan government of coming collapse; Ghani government refuses to support resistance
Taliban repeatedly offer Massoud the foreign minister post; he conditions acceptance on elections, Taliban say that is against Islam
Taliban-run Afghanistan reportedly building ~5 jihadi madrasas per district (~2,000 total)
Vienna conference of Afghan opposition groups; no state funded or supported it

key_claims: Al-Qaeda assassinated Ahmad Shah Massoud on 9 Sept 2001 precisely because a Massoud–US coalition would doom the Taliban and AQ.

The Taliban are more extreme than in the 1990s because they spent 20 years integrated with al-Qaeda and trained by regional intelligence agencies; AQ members have married into senior Taliban families.
Al-Qaeda 'localized' jihad: Taliban for Afghanistan, TTP for Pakistan, Jamaat Ansarullah for Tajikistan, IMU for Uzbekistan all operate within AQ's orbit under different banners.
The Taliban are building ~5 jihadi madrasas per district (~2,000), a recruitment pipeline the UN underestimates.
Most ISKP in Afghanistan is aligned with the Taliban (e.g. Kunduz); Taliban–IS clashes in the southeast are about power, not ideology.

Panjshir fell in 3 weeks (15 Aug–6 Sept 2021) because it had been demilitarised (tourist destination, DDR disarmament, no mines) and <1,000 fighters faced ~35,000 Taliban plus TTP, Arab AQ, Tajik, Uzbek and Pakistani fighters, running out of ammunition.
Ghani's government refused to back any resistance; NDS chief Saraj said Ghani preferred a Taliban takeover to Massoud standing.
The NRF wants Taliban designated a terror group, recognition of Afghan democratic forces, and a fraction of past material support — no foreign boots; basing should be Tajikistan not Pakistan.
Resistance groups (NRF, AFF, AUF, Green Trend) share 'horizontal unity'; disunity and civil-war warnings are pro-Taliban scare tactics.
